cards.note: On the 60, east of Fiambalá, bright red mountains line the road, sometimes quite dramatically. A few of the red hills are embedded in between gray hills in a way that almost looks like a badly colored black and white photograph. Good luck telling it apart from similar roads in Salta and La Rioja! The best method may be the clouds: This road has no clouds, while the one in La Rioja has some low hazy ones to the South (except when it doesn't) and the one in Salta has higher, better defined clouds. It's tough.

In La Rioja, just north of Talampaya National Park, there is a part of the RN40 with almost blindingly bright red mountains. Good luck telling it apart from similar roads in Catamarca and Salta! The best method may be the clouds: This road has low clouds toward the South (except when it doesn't), while the one in Catamarca is always cloudless and the one in Salta has higher, better defined clouds. It's tough.

In the North of Neuquén, the Google driver started their day early and the camera did not like it. As the day progresses, the car goes further north and the glitchy colors fade, until only a bit of color noise remains, and finally, around the province border, it starts to look like normal footage.

On the 68 in Salta, between Alemania and Cafayate, there's a stretch of red mountains. Compared to the red mountains in La Rioja and Catamarca, the surrounding range is more massive and the red not quite as cartoonish. You may also be able to tell the difference by the clouds: The ones here are high above and relatively defined; the ones in La Rioja, when they appear, are low in the southern sky and kind of hazy, and the coverage in Catamarca is cloudless.
On the 65 in Tucuman, leading west to the Catamarca border near Parque Nacional Aconquija, the Google car drove through what appears to be mist thick enough to clog your windpipe.
Northeast of La Paz, there is an unpaved road that is cloudy and wet and narrow and looks like a nightmare to drive. Yet, apparently, it is frequented by mountain bikers a whole lot.
Gen 4 coverage in the state of Amapá has a distinct blur in the front right of the panorama. Make sure you have the striped car.
Brown mushroom insulators appear in (mostly urban) Pernambuco.

cards.a: Brazil - East of Belo QR Code
cards.note: A small region just east of Belo Horizonte has a little QR code sticker on almost every pole that's found nowhere else in the country.

In the states of Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba and Pernambuco, these two types of insulators on thin stems can be found. One looks like a thick cone that gets thinner toward the bottom, and the other has a sort of rounded silhouette - careful, it's easy to confuse with another insulator that can also be found elsewhere, with three equal width ridges. The bottom ridge has to be substantially smaller in order to create the round shape.

cards.a: Brazil - Maranhao black and white pickup
cards.note: In northern Maranhao, Google used a recognizable pickup truck with a white cab and a black bed for some footage around Lencois Maranhenses National Park

If you see a little square black dot low on the flat side of a ladder pole, you're going to be in Paraná. Other states may have unpainted square indents, some white or silver dots/stickers, but only in Paraná is it ever black. Its absence does not mean you are not in Paraná, and it appears to be a relatively new practice (found mostly on newer poles).
In rural Maranhao, you will often see trident poles with large, UFO-like insulators. These insulators are common elsewhere as well, but with the trident config it's going to be Maranhao.
The white mushroom insulators are typical for Bahia, but I also found some on the southern border of Pernambuco. They are generally more common in urban areas than in rural ones.

Yellow center lines in Saskatchewan frequently have tiny white bits in and around them. You can also rarely find them in BC and Yukon, but the landscape there should be different enough to not get them confused.
In Arica and Iquique, in the very North of Chile, sometimes there'll be a little stick with a few leaves stuck on the car's back.
On the tiny Isla de Providencia, Google used a small silver truck with a long antenna
The northern tip of Colombia looks a lot like Tumbes and Piura in Peru, but with more cacti and a different car
On the small island of San Andrés, Google used a small white truck with no antenna
One road on the southern east coast of Ecuador looks a lot like a gray, dirty, depressing version of Tumbes or Piura, just with more garbage. It has an offshoot with a pretty beach.
All-green painted metal poles can be found in only a few areas of Guatemala, mostly in the Southeast of the country. They have codes on them that will tell you even more precisely where you are.

If you see red-white-red-white stripes on trees (and rarely poles) that line the road, you will be in Bihar (other regions have similar markings with just three stripes). The paint is often faded considerably.

4 Yellow-black-yellow-black stripes on poles will usually place you in Bihar. Also appears in Delhi sometimes, but it's much more commonly 5 or more stripes there. 5 and 3 stripes can also rarely be found in Bihar.
5 or more black&yellow stripes on poles are usually only a Delhi thing. Rarely appears in other places, like Bihar. Sometimes, you will find fewer than 5 stripes on poles in Delhi.
Many Kerala poles have a particular yellow marking, usually round, with hand-written Latin script in black.
Mint green to grayish-green electricity counters of this particular design are found in Punjab and Haryana.
Poles and trees in Tamil Nadu have a particular white-black-white marking.
A car with a big black cab and an open back in which a variety of people ride is found in eastern Bali, south of Mount Agung
A car with black railings and (usually) a big wooden stake lying in the bed can be found in eastern Bali, south of Mount Agung

Aomori road paint diamonds:

  • Full size
  • Two L shapes overlapping clockwise on the wide angles

Kagawa road paint diamonds:

  • Full size
  • Kung Fu salutation pattern

Nara and Wakayama road paint diamonds:

  • Full size
  • Four elements arranged to overlap clockwise

(Mostly northern) Nara road paint diamonds:

  • Snack size
  • Four elements arranged to overlap clockwise

Saga road paint diamonds:

  • Snack size & skinny
  • Diamond broken in the middle

Shizuoka road paint diamonds:

  • Skinny
  • Kung Fu salutation pattern

Yamanashi and Nagano road paint diamonds:

  • Skinny
  • Four elements arranged to overlap counter-clockwise
Only on a very tiny bit of coverage on the C104 in southern Kenya, embedded in Tsavo National Park, the Google car is adorned with two recognizable splats of bird poop. Cheers.
A tiny bit of footage near Gunung Mulu National Park, south of Brunei, was shot with a long silver truck with a chrome rollcage and three logos on the hood

In the state of Jalisco, it is common to see poles painted Taiwan style with a black and yellow barberpole pattern, or Kansai style with long vertical black and yellow stripes. Careful: these can very rarely appear in other states
North and south of Altai, the Google car in Gen 4 has its tent tied down with four neatly packed straps. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
On a short stretch of the road leading to Ulaangrom in the Northwest of the country, east of Tarialan, there is a black object visible on the left side of the truck bed. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are four straps visible, you will be on the eastern part of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

On a road in northeastern Mongolia, the Google car drove through sunset into nighttime. There is a second road in the southeast with sunset coverage, which can be distinguished by the driving angle: this one goes east, the one in the South goes north.

In southeastern Mongolia, the Google car drove until after sunset. You can see the shadows becoming longer and the footage eventually turns very dark. This can be told apart from the other sunset road in the northeast by the driving angle - this one goes north, the other one goes east.
From Bayankhongor to Arvaikheer, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot. The mess is one clump with no loose loops. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
From Arvaikheer to Ulaanbaatar, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot that has a loose loop. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

Between Altai and Bayankhongor, Gen 4 coverage will have two straps with a messy knot. While further east, the zipper tag is a bit more central, on this part of the road it is all the way left. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are four straps converging into a single point on the left side, you will be on a north-south bit in the middle of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

The zipper of tent on the Google car is open on a stretch of road between Tosontsengel and the Teel area. When there are just two straps visible, you will be on the westernmost part of that coverage. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
West of Altai until about Sharga, the Google car in Gen 4 has its tent tied down with two neatly packed straps, no knots. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

In the West and Northwest of the country, the tent on the car in Gen4 coverage is usually tied with two straps and a single knot visible in the center of the tent or to the left. When the knot is slightly on the right of the tent, you will be on one specific road between Durvuljin and Uliastai. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

In the Southwest of the country, the tent on the car in Gen4 coverage is usually tied with two straps and two knots on the right side. If the knots are on the left instead, you will be on one of two specific stretches of road around the Tarvagatai Mountains. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
Between Khotont and Lun, you will find four straps tying down the tent on the Google car in Gen4, with both knots on the right side. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc

cards.a: Mongolia - Two knots, one center (4 straps)
cards.note: Around Tsetserleg, you will find four straps tying down the tent on the Google car in Gen4, with one of the two knots in the center of the tent and the other one on the right side. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
Between Khyargas Lake and Songino, a water bottle will be visible on the left side of the truck bed. Info from fuzziejaxer's doc
Black vertical pole markings with 7 digits that start with 1 or 4 (or rarely 3) are found only in western central North Island.

cards.a: New Zealand - Auckland and Northland pole code
cards.note: If you see a black vertical pole code with six or seven digits, with or without an extra tag, that starts with a 9, you are going to be in Auckland or further north.
Between the two rivers around Christchurch, you can find 5-character pole codes that start with two letters. They are a little smaller than the vertical black codes in other parts of the country.

cards.a: New Zealand - Northern tip pole code
cards.note: Only on the northernmost tip of Northland will you find six-digit-plus-tag pole codes that start with a 2
An area in southeastern Manawatu has pole codes with a P followed by 5 digits

cards.a: New Zealand - Red White Blue Dots
cards.note: On the northeast tip of Northland, you will find little pole stickers in red, white and blue (although not always all three). They can be round or rectangular.
There are just three areas on North Island with these specific warning stickers on electricity poles
A 6-digits-plus-tag pole code starting with 30 or 31 with inverted colors (black on white) means you are in Auckland or Northland
Benin City has these two unique follow cars: a black and a wine red Toyota SUV without police markings.

In southern and eastern North Macedonia, some roads have recognizable smudges on the camera: A large dead insect on the R1205, a vertical pattern of about four smudges on the PS27, a central smudge (plus more further south) on the easternmost part of the A3, a brown smudge on the lower left center in the southeast of the country, and on the A1 to Bitola, a single smudge higher up to the left with a short section of two brown smudges center left halfway between Bitola and Prilep
A vertical white sticker with blue or red numbers places you in Arequipa Province
In the wider Cusco area and up to the tri-point with Brazil and Bolivia, concrete poles will sometimes have yellow stickers with black numbers going sideways.
East of Chimbote, there's a road where sundown and clouds conspired to create footage as if from the depths (or rather heights?) of hell.
Around the town of Locumba, between Moquegua and Tacna, you get bollards that look like half-buried Moquegua type, interspersed with sections with just loose white rocks for bollards.
These round white bollards with orange and black markings at the top are only found around the southern Department of Moquegua

Bollards with the same color scheme as the Moquegua ones, but in different prism shapes (triangular, quadrangular) and/or with white and red reflectors appear on the 38A through Tacla and Puno and on the 3S south of Ilave. If they appear in Gen 3 coverage, go Ilo (on the coast)
If you see a white sticker with blue text on a pole, you will be in the very south, below Arequipa
Sandy soil, fairly flat, green or withered bushes.
Two horizontal yellow stickers with black text can be found on concrete poles in a corridor between Tingo Maria and Ayacucho.
Super flat desert (a bit hilly northwest though), sandy, sparse bushes

In an area including Bicol, Catanduanes and Masbate, you will see guardrails marked with three black stripes. Careful: you can get more or fewer than three in other places as well, but if you see three, it is most likely going to be this area.
The stems on which insulators sit at the top of poles is commonly thick or encased in a plastic tube that makes it appear much thicker than usual on the island of Bohol.

cards.a: Philippines - Davao Occidental quad pancake insulator
cards.note: If you see a quadruple pancake insulator on a pole top, you're going to be on the one road with coverage in Davao Occidental, along the coast, between approximately Don Marcelino and Bukid.

cards.a: Philippines - East Samar double pancake insulator
cards.note: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.

cards.a: Philippines - Ilocos Norte and Biliran quad insulator
cards.note: This cylinder with four distinct ridges is most common in Ilocos Norte, but can also be found in southern Biliran.

cards.a: Philippines - Manila and Ilocos Norte Star Wars insulator
cards.note: This type of insulator that looks like the buildings on Tatooine is most common in northern Luzon and in and around Manila.
This grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks kind of solid is most common in and around Manila, but can rarely be found elsewhere.
Flimsy mesh poles are common in the province of Zamboanga Sibugay. They also, rarely, appear in other provinces, but even then you should be on Mindanao.

In northern Cebu, you will find gray concrete guard blocks with their edges or sides painted yellow. These are not the only guard blocks in the area, so don't discount northern Cebu if you see, for example, fully yellow concrete blocks or walls and blocks with diagonal black and yellow stripes.
Chile poles can be frequently found in northern Luzon, especially Cagayan, but careful - they can also appear, if less commonly, in northern Negros!

cards.a: Philippines - Northwest Leyte and Biliran extender insulators
cards.note: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in northwestern Leyte and northwestern Biliran.
The trikes on the island of Palawan are recognizable by their single wide front window. Many of them look as if they were cosplaying as cars, with emblems and everything.
On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.
In a small area on the isthmus of Quezon province, you will find alternating red and blue guard blocks.

In southern Mindanao, in the very South of the Philippines, there is some footage taken with a silver truck with a visible roof rack. Note that this is leftover, unculled old coverage that runs parallel to gen 4 images of the same locations, so you can still get the same roads with a different car.

The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.
In Limpopo, northeast of Polokwane, there are yellow boulders lying around as if a giant dropped his toys.
